PROV-O: carrying out a manufacturing operation is an activity.
PROV-O: a traceable piece of material is a physical entity.
PROV-O: a direct material input is a specific source of derivation.
PROV-O: the producing operation is the activity that generated this piece.
SOSA 2017: material taken from a heat or piece represents the sampled material.
SOSA 2017: measuring a steelmaking or product characteristic is an observation.
The sample represents the heat or piece from which the material was taken.
The heat or piece is the feature whose property was observed.
The measurement item code identifies the property observed in a reading.
SOSA 2017: a sampling timestamp can locate the observed phenomenon in time. The local value is a dateTime literal; SOSA links to a temporal entity.
SOSA 2017: both use dateTime. Result availability corresponds to activity completion only when the two events coincide.
EPCIS 2.0.1: input and output identities describe the split of one coil into new coils.
EPCIS 2.0.1: packing identified coils under one package identifier creates a physical aggregation.
EPCIS 2.0.1: a scan that observes an identified piece at a receiving or shipping point corresponds to an object event.
